newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway stocks inch up but starved for impulses.
newsitem.headline: Norway stocks inch up but starved for impulses.

text.p: Norwegian shares closed slightly higher in moderate trade on Wednesday.
"What we need now is probably lower interest rates and more impulses from overseas," said one dealer. "It is quiet abroad too."
The Total index closed 4.4 points up at 825.5 points, an increase of 0.53 percent, in turnover worth 644 million crowns.
Food-based conglomerate Orkla, the second biggest company listed on the stock exchange, rosed a hefty 9.5 crowns to 354 crowns.
The share fell five crowns on Monday, following a local newspaper story that the company's letter of intent for bottling Coca-Cola could be in jeopardy.
"I believe the share's fall on Monday was unjustified, and the story was greatly exaggerated," said one dealer.
Telecommunications company ASK climbed 2.50 crowns, or 5.6 percent, to 47.00 crowns.
"It seems like technology shares are a bit revitalised, many investors have increased confidence in the sector," said another dealer.
